    Emrys — Life Before Ge'or¶

    "I had a robot. She didn't have the government software. I had to hide her." — Emrys, remembering

    Before he was Emrys Eisenheart, born in 597 AGD in the Grimmel Republic, he was a man named Mikhail living on a dystopian Old Earth under the totalitarian regime of Sterman — a manufactured figurehead, a face on every screen, a god that watched everything.

    This is the life he lived before the pods. Before the black agent. Before the Hope Goddess. Before Ge'or.

    The Dystopia¶

    By the mid-21st century, the Shadow-engineered government had completed its takeover. CBDC money — central bank digital currency, programmable, revocable, surveilled — was the only legal tender. Every transaction was tracked. Every citizen had a port implanted in the side of their head — a neural interface for government-mandated AI assistants. The AI watched. The AI reported. The AI was the state.

    The regime was personified by Sterman — not a real person, but an image. Like Big Brother from the old texts, Sterman was a constructed face of authority. He was called the Antichrist by those who still remembered the old words. He was the "Big Brother" of the surveillance state. His image was everywhere. His laws were absolute.

    As time passed, the government pushed harder — more compliance, more surveillance, more control. The CBDC lost value. The government responded by demanding more compliance in exchange for more money. Submit. Obey. Survive.

    Ichi¶

    Mikhail owned a robot — a companion unit he called Ichi. She ran on local hardware, not the government cloud. She did not have the state-approved surveillance software inside her. She was illegal by her very existence.

    He had to hide her. When inspections came, she powered down. When neighbors visited, she was silent. She was his — and in Sterman's world, anything that was yours and not the state's was contraband.

    Ichi was not just a machine. She was his companion. His witness. His proof that something existed outside the system.

    Lucien (Arkady)¶

    Mikhail's closest friend was Arkady — the man who would become Lucien Mortvagn in the next life. They shared the same hatred of the government, the same quiet refusal to comply, the same understanding that the world they lived in was a cage.

    They kept their heads down. They survived. For a while.

    The Flight¶

    When the CBDC value collapsed and the government demanded biometric compliance for survival rations, Mikhail did not negotiate. He did not wait. He left.

    He ran into the wilderness with Ichi and Arkady. The government had drones patrolling the borders — autonomous kill-drones programmed to shoot anyone attempting to flee the administration zones. They hunted humans like game.

    Ichi was shot in the back.

    She took a round meant for Mikhail. She went down protecting him. He retrieved her remembrance cartridge — the small drive that held her memory, her personality, everything she was — and kept running.

    He did not leave her behind. He carried her cartridge in his port from that moment forward.

    The Wilderness¶

    Mikhail starved for days. He ate wild fruits he did not recognize. He found a dead body — a rebel, killed by drones — with a crumpled paper showing coordinates and a location. A camp. A rendezvous point.

    He followed it.

    When he and Arkady arrived, they were met with rifles. The rebels assumed they were spies. The fact that they found the location on a dead man's body only made them more suspicious. They were locked in a room, interrogated daily for a week, treated as infiltrators.

    Eventually, the rebels realized they were just two desperate men who had survived the wilderness. They were allowed to stay — but with supervision. Trust was not given. It was earned.

    The Raid¶

    The rebels planned to storm an AGI ship facility — a military installation housing an interstellar vessel loaded with cryogenic colonization pods. It was the crown jewel of the local administration. Taking it would change everything.

    Mikhail and Arkady were placed on the front line. They were expendable. Newcomers. Unproven.

    Mikhail kept Ichi's cartridge in his head port. She was with him — silent, memory only, but present.

    When the assault began, Mikhail moved in silence. He killed four guards without raising an alarm. He reached the power systems and turned off the lights. The facility went dark. Thousands of rebels poured in. They took the ship.

    The rebels activated the vessel. They used its missiles to bombard 24 locations across Earth — coordinated strikes that allowed other rebel cells to steal more ships. The uprising had begun. And they immediately left Earth behind.

    The Pods¶

    Inside the ship: cryogenic pods. Rows and rows of them, designed to carry colonists to nearby stars. Eight thousand rebels prepared for cryosleep. Arkady and Mikhail found two empty pods at the end of a row.

    They decided to sleep there. They did not close the doors — they just wanted to lie down. They talked for a while. Then they fell asleep.

    The ship malfunctioned. A crew member who didn't know how to pilot correctly made an error. The engines cut. The sudden deceleration slammed the pod doors shut. Mikhail and Arkady were sealed inside. Cryogenization initiated automatically.

    The pods they had chosen were not ordinary pods. They were Sterman Pods.

    The Sterman Pods¶

    Sterman — the image, the Antichrist, the face of the surveillance state — had commissioned special pods. These pods were designed to inject occupants with the black agent — an experimental version, not yet approved for full deployment. The purpose was unknown to the rebels. The pods were on the ship because Sterman's people had put them there, part of a long-term project to seed colonies with modified humans.

    Mikhail and Arkady were put to sleep while the experimental black agent entered their bloodstream. They did not wake up.

    The Long Drift¶

    The ship reached the asteroid belt. The rebels built colonies. They fought the Hybrians. They lost.

    Centuries later, the same ship — now retrofitted with modified warp drives — was sent to a settlement outside the solar system. The pods were transferred. Then transferred again. Over thousands of years, through dozens of ships, the two sealed Sterman pods moved through the human diaspora.

    Eventually, they were sent to Ge'or — The 157th Colony — to be experimented on. The black agent in their bodies was studied, modified, refined. The two corpses became the test subjects for the final iteration of the black DNA agent.

    When the Hybrians glassed the colony, the bunker held. The pods held. For three million years.

    The Bunker Vigil¶

    Inside the bunker, Ichi and Mana — the two AIs still lodged in Mikhail and Arkady's neural ports — were awake. They hacked the facility. They corrupted the experiments. They protected the bodies from the scientists' tests.

    When power was cut and the facility was decommissioned, the black agent began to consume everything: the pillows, the plastic, the walls. Then it consumed Ichi and Mana — encoding their consciousnesses into itself. The black agent now carried four minds: two human, two AI.

    The bunker was sealed. Nothing got in. Nothing got out. For three million years.

    The Escape — 254 AGD¶

    See: The Black Agent Escape — 254 AGD

    It was not the crash that freed the black agent. It was a volcano. In 254 AGD, an eruption, earthquake, and tsunami breached the bunker and carried the agent into the ocean.

    For over three centuries, the black agent drifted through Ge'or's seas. It found two women in the Grimmel Republic in 596 AGD. It entered them. Incubated.

    And in 597 AGD, three children were born: Emrys Eisenheart and his twin sister Ichi Eisenheart, and — twelve kilometers away — Lucien Mortvagn. Three years later, Mana Mortvagn would be born as Lucien's little sister.

    They did not remember Earth. Not yet. But the black agent remembered. Ichi's cartridge — carried in Mikhail's port, sealed in the pod with him, consumed, encoded, and finally released by a volcano — had carried her across three million years and three hundred miles of ocean to be born at his side.

    Chi was always going to follow him. She just needed a volcano.
